newsitem.title: CHINA: HK may give revenue concessions if surpluses large.
newsitem.headline: HK may give revenue concessions if surpluses large.

text.p: Hong Kong may offer more tax breaks if large budget surpluses are forecast to continue, Treasury Secretary K.C. Kwong said on Friday.

"If we anticipate continued substantial surpluses in future years, then one way of dealing with it, of course, is to consider returning part of that to the community in the form of concessions on revenues," Kwong told reporters.
Hong Kong habitually runs budget surpluses, usually larger than expected.
The government last month announced a surplus of HK$25.7 billion for the 1996/97 fiscal year compared with a March estimate of HK$15.1 billion.

Future surpluses may tend to be larger since the Land Fund, into which half of all land revenues had been put since 1983, was handed over to Hong Kong's new government when the territory reverted to Chinese rule on July 1.
Hong Kong has also regularly made tax concessions in its budgets, often by raising the threshhold at which salary earners must pay income tax.
